svg.title: Thymosin alpha-1: 60 years from thymus extract to FDA “no”
svg.desc: Timeline. 1966: Goldstein lab describes “thymosin,” a thymus factor tied to lymphocyte production. 1977: Thymosin alpha-1 isolated from “fraction 5” and sequenced: 28 amino acids. 1979: Lab synthetic version as active as the natural one; fraction 5 also held ubiquitin. 1980: Made in E. coli from a synthetic gene (Biochemistry). 1999: U.S. hepatitis B trial: 14% vs 4% response, not significant (P=0.084). 2010: Melanoma trial, 488 people: some response signal; survival P=0.08. 2016: SciClone: Zadaxin sales $150.1M, about 95% of revenue from China. 2017: SciClone acquired for $11.18 a share in cash. 2024: FDA advisers vote 17–4 against adding it to the 503A bulks list. 2025: TESTS sepsis trial, 1,106 people: no survival benefit (BMJ). 2026: FDA lists it as “nominated but withdrawn”; new sepsis mechanism trial posted.
